summary.one_liner: Motrix is a desktop download manager (Electron app) for HTTP, FTP, BitTorrent and magnet links, with a headless Docker server option and a browser extension.
summary.what_it_does: Motrix is a desktop download manager for HTTP, FTP, BitTorrent, and magnet links, built on a Motrix-maintained fork of the aria2 download engine. The README describes the v2 "Motrix Turbo" rewrite in Electron, React, and TypeScript, with a download core separate from the UI. It supports per-file BitTorrent selection, tracker list management, UPnP/NAT-PMP port mapping, upload and download limits with speed profiles, and SQLite-backed sessions that restore downloads after restart. A headless server mode runs on Node.js or Docker with a web UI, and the official @motrix/cli command-line client and browser extensions (Chrome, Edge, Firefox) hand downloads to the app over the MDXP JSON-RPC protocol. Plugins run in a QuickJS sandbox with declared permissions and an in-app marketplace.
use_cases: manage HTTP, FTP and BitTorrent downloads on a desktop
download torrents and magnet links with per-file selection
run a download server on a NAS or home server with Docker
send browser downloads to a desktop download manager
control downloads from the command line or scripts
limit download and upload speed with profiles
how_to_run: mkdir -p motrix-data downloads && sudo chown 1000:1000 motrix-data downloads
git clone <repository URL> && cd Motrix && pnpm install && pnpm start
notable: MDXP (Motrix Download eXchange Protocol), a JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol used by the browser extension and CLI
Headless Docker server with device-code pairing for remote CLI and agent clients
Plugins run in a QuickJS sandbox with user-approved permissions and an in-app marketplace
Desktop app runs on macOS, Windows and Linux, including Snap, Flatpak, AppImage, deb, rpm and pacman packages
Motrix Extension for Chrome, Edge and Firefox hands browser downloads to Motrix
caveats: Windows x64 and arm64 packages are unsigned and may trigger SmartScreen warnings
The README says all 32-bit packages remain unavailable

Motrix 2.1.0 migration from v1 imports tasks as paused and recommends backing up the existing profile first; Windows in-place BitTorrent activation needs a supported NTFS volume and explicit authorization
Internet access to the headless server requires a TLS reverse proxy and firewall rules; insecure HTTP operator mode is intended only for trusted LANs
keywords: download torrents on mac windows linux
